To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the accounting measure of dilution is a positive predictor of future EPS and that investors use this information prior to its disclosure at the earnings announcement.

the dilutive adjustment captures the partial resolution of uncertainty attached to growth stocks, and that investors do not use the information disclosed in the dilutive adjustments at the earnings announcement.

the accounting measures of earnings dilution do not have any predictive power for future earnings or stock returns and the market does not use information from the fully diluted EPS at earnings announcement date.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the dilutive adjustment relates to the earnings process and the stock return process.

understanding why the dilutive adjustment appears to be a good predictor of future EPS and why the information in this measure is apparently not useful for explaining unexpected returns at earnings announcement date.
the information content of Canadian accounting measures of dilutive securities and the extent to which this information is used by investors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the accounting measures of earnings dilution have no explanatory power for the earnings process and for stock returns.

the dilutive adjustment appears to be a useful measure for investors to predict the earnings process, but it does not provide any additional information that is useful to investors in the pricing process.
the accounting measures of earnings dilution are not informative to investors and are not used in the valuation process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accounting measures of earnings dilution have explanatory power for earnings and stock returns, but the information is not used by investors at the announcement date.
the accounting measure of earnings dilution does not appear to be a useful tool in predicting future earnings.
the traditional view that the dilutive adjustment presents the investor with bad earnings news due to the potential dilution of earnings is not supported by the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
accounting measures of dilutive earnings can be misleading.
the accounting measure of earnings dilution is not a reliable indicator of bad news.
the dilutive adjustment under pre-2000 Canadian GAAP is not a good proxy for dilution.
